tldr: For iid observational data with uniform covariates, bounded potential outcomes, and a treated mean in the exact whole-space \(\mathcal H^\beta(L)\) ball, the global envelope \(P\{e(X)\leq t\}\leq Ct^{\gamma-1}\) permits arbitrary measurable propensities and within-cell treated concentration. Fixed polynomial-norming subcells stabilize every occupied balanced fit; the ambient Taylor approximation covers boundary cells, and ordered subcell masses and binomial tails retain empty cells without a logarithmic loss. With \(D=d\gamma/(\gamma-1)\) and the exact width \(h_n=2^{-\lceil\log n/\{(2\beta+D)\log2\}\rceil}\), the estimator and the pinned bounded binary converse give \(c n^{-\beta/(2\beta+D)}\leq\mathfrak R_n\leq K n^{-\beta/(2\beta+D)}\) for every integer \(n\geq1\). The single count-only selector uses neither \(\gamma\) nor \(C\) and attains this rate for all sufficiently large \(n\) in each fixed compatible tail class. In the smooth-control CATE subclass, under \(C(1-\kappa)^q\geq1\), the contrast estimator at this same exact width has its upper bound and the zero-control submodel has its matching minimax lower bound for every integer \(n\geq1\).
gap: Dorn's Theorem 1 obtains the log-free weak-overlap sup-norm frontier under a local nonconcentration assumption and explicitly leaves a degeneracy-robust estimator outside scope. A global propensity-tail envelope alone does not imply that assumption.
fill: Balanced polynomial-norming subcells replace stochastic raw-design conditioning by deterministic geometry. An ordered-mass inequality then converts the single global tail budget into a summable collection of local count tails, producing a same-class upper bound and bounded-outcome converse.
